steps.label: TIMELINESS
steps.sub: is about the data's relationship to time

steps.label: STILL CAN FAIL
steps.sub: even if accurate, valid, and consistent

steps.label: FRESHNESS
steps.sub: how old is this data vs. its update cadence?

steps.label: LATENCY
steps.sub: how long from real-world event to landing here?

code:
SELECT
    ProductId, LastUpdated,
    DATEDIFF(HOUR, LastUpdated, GETDATE())
        AS HoursSinceUpdate
FROM dbo.Inventory
WHERE DATEDIFF(HOUR, LastUpdated, GETDATE()) > 24;
caption: Every inventory row not refreshed in more than 24 hours.

code:
SELECT
    OrderId, OrderPlacedAt, LoadedIntoWarehouseAt,
    DATEDIFF(MINUTE, OrderPlacedAt,
              LoadedIntoWarehouseAt) AS LatencyMinutes
FROM dbo.OrderLoadLog
WHERE DATEDIFF(MINUTE, OrderPlacedAt,
                LoadedIntoWarehouseAt) > 15;
caption: A timeliness failure even when every other value in the row is flawless.

code:
SELECT
    CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN DATEDIFF(HOUR, LastUpdated,
                  GETDATE()) <= 24
             THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DECIMAL(5,2))
        / COUNT(*) * 100 AS FreshnessRatePct
FROM dbo.Inventory;
caption: The same aggregate-to-a-percentage pattern used for every dimension this chapter.

subtitle: Turning six dimensions into formal, repeatable rules.
